evidence.excerpt: Switch-mode power supplies (SMPS) are tested for conducted emissions according to CISPR 32 using three commercially available line impedance stabilisation networks (LISNs) of nominally identical 50 Ω/50 µH topology but from different manufacturers. Tests are performed on five SMPS samples with rated power between 30 W and 250 W. Measured quasi-peak levels at the same SMPS unit differ by up to 7.2 dB across LISNs in the 150 kHz to 500 kHz band, exceeding the 3 dB reproducibility figure often cited in the literature. The observed discrepancies are traced to differences in the LISN high-frequency impedance characteristic, particularly a self-resonance near 1.4 MHz in one unit. An additional test campaign varies the mains source impedance from 0.05 Ω to 0.8 Ω at 50 Hz by inserting series inductors, demonstrating that SMPS peak emission levels shift by up to 5 dB due to changes in rectifier operating point. These findings have implications for compliance margins and for the interpretation of borderline-pass test results.
